svg.text: Hover needs to answer: which point (or link) is under the cursor?
Asking the GPU per mouse move used to cost O(elements).
Each pixel stores [point index, x, y]; empty pixels hold −1.
Rendered by the GPU for all pixels at once, at half resolution.
Each pixel stores [link index, 0, 0, validity]; alpha 0 = empty.
Same link draw shader, switched to index mode (renderMode = 1).
a 1-pixel-wide link would fall between half-res texels.
links are thin, so no window scan or nearest-candidate logic.
a fully transparent link writes nothing and cannot be hovered.
the dash mask applies only to the visible pass, so dashed links
are pickable along their whole length, gaps included.
the hovered link is re-drawn wider in this buffer, so it is easier
to keep a link hovered than to acquire it.
the link result applies only when no point was picked. Here the
cursor sits on link 4, but point 3 from the 9×9 window takes priority.
Re-rendered only when marked stale: points move, data or config
changes, zoom, resize — plus hover changes, which invalidate the
link buffer only (the hovered link is drawn wider there). Read
back asynchronously (PBO + fence) — hover never stalls the GPU.
The maps refresh only when the scene changes — a still scene does no picking work. A hover then reads 81 pixels for points
and 1 pixel for links, so it costs the same at 300 elements or 300,000.
